B goes further on concrete fixes: seeding deliberately wrong suggestions, warning that a wrong explanation can increase trust in a wrong answer, logging confirms and changes separately, and pointing out that rubber-stamped labels contaminate retraining data. A is stronger on weighing throughput through its explicit A/B pilot, but neither answer says which parts of the current screen to keep, such as the side-by-side claim text and dropdown. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers read the 9% against the 2% the same way, name the pre-selection and save-on-Next mechanism, and propose similar measure-then-fix steps. B weighs the throughput cost more directly: it pilots blind review as an A/B test to check whether the accuracy gain is worth the extra time, and it quantifies severity, including the 3.5x figure and the yearly total. A adds useful points about retraining contamination and misleading explanations, but neither answer says which parts of the current screen to keep.
